northstar: DB/SIF/Vision/Ontology/Learning이 실제 위험성평가와 TBM 결과를 바꾸고, 공유 가능 여부까지 통제하는 상업제품 수준 workbench
qualityChecks: npm.cmd test -- tests/workpack-readiness.test.ts tests/commercial-harness.test.ts tests/quality-contract.test.ts tests/operation-improvements.test.ts tests/photo-vision-analysis.test.ts

userStories.title: Separate generated workpack from share-ready workpack
acceptance: Generated documents can still show review-required when DB harness, ontology, quality, or placeholder checks are not ready.
Share UI receives a user-facing disabled reason instead of treating 12/12 documents as ready.
Focused unit test proves warning workpacks are blocked from normal dispatch.

userStories.title: Make DB harness output visible in generated deliverables
acceptance: Accepted photo/improvement memory appears inside risk assessment, TBM briefing, TBM log, and photo evidence drafts.
Provider fallback/template paths remain DB-harness-first and do not leak generic fallback prose.
Focused test proves document body changes when harnessMemory includes an improvement.

userStories.title: Prepare SIF embedding approval gate without mutating DB
acceptance: Approval packet states record counts, corpus hash, migration requirement, and no DB mutation performed.
Operator report explains that actual embedding upload is not done until explicit approval.

userStories.title: Turn photo Vision/OCR candidates into deterministic safety rows
acceptance: Accepted input photo candidates create deterministic hazard/control seed rows before LLM prose.
Before/After improvement photos are exportable to md/jsonl learning files.
Focused tests cover photo candidate acceptance and learning export.

userStories.title: Expose operating ontology as list and hover-card graph
acceptance: Workspace shows Workpack -> Hazard -> Control -> Improvement -> Evidence -> Ack relationships in user language.
List view and hover-card graph work without Hermes or LangGraph core replacement.
Browser check captures desktop and mobile ontology surfaces.

userStories.title: Unify every product page under the workspace design language
acceptance: Workspace typography feels more grounded on the first screen.
Non-workspace product pages stop using the old marketing-heavy design guide where it conflicts with the workspace.
Browser screenshots prove desktop and mobile readability.
